analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The repository is small enough that all four tracked files and both notebooks were inspected rather than sampled. The checkout was supplied with a depth-50 recent-history constraint, which can truncate larger histories; local Git reports a non-shallow repository and exposes only four commits, suggesting the available history fits within that limit, but no unavailable history was assumed.

stated_purpose: Analyze a Pymaceuticals mouse-study dataset by cleaning duplicate observations, comparing drug regimens statistically, visualizing treatment and demographic data, evaluating final tumor-volume outliers, and modeling the relationship between mouse weight and tumor volume.

observed_capabilities.statement: The completed notebook imports pandas, Matplotlib, and SciPy, reads two expected CSV datasets, and merges mouse metadata with longitudinal study results by Mouse ID.
The notebook identifies duplicate Mouse ID/timepoint records, removes mouse g989, and produces descriptive tumor-volume statistics grouped by drug regimen.

The notebook contains bar charts, sex-distribution pie charts, regimen-specific box plots, a Capomulin mouse time-series plot, a weight-versus-tumor-volume scatter plot, outlier calculations, Pearson correlation, and linear regression.
Saved outputs report 249 original mice, 248 after removing g989, one potential Infubinol outlier, and a 0.84 correlation for the Capomulin weight/tumor-volume calculation.

planned_work.statement: Unfilled template prompts indicate intended but unfinished work: an aggregation-based summary-statistics implementation, a combined four-regimen box plot, and three written analytical conclusions.

architecture.statement: The repository is a notebook-only data-analysis project: pymaceuticals_starter_guided.ipynb provides the guided exercise structure, while main.ipynb contains the attempted implementation and embedded outputs.

The workflow expects two local CSV files under data/, merges them into an in-memory pandas DataFrame, performs cleaning and grouped statistical calculations, and renders charts inline through Matplotlib.
There is no packaged application, reusable Python module, persistent data store, service boundary, or automated execution layer.

accomplishments.statement: A guided notebook was extended into a substantially executed analysis covering data preparation, descriptive statistics, demographic and treatment plots, outlier detection, and correlation/regression.
The committed notebook preserves 11 inline PNG visualizations and contains no saved execution-error output.

gaps.statement: The two CSV inputs referenced by both notebooks are not tracked, so the analysis cannot be rerun from this repository alone.
The README contains only the repository title and provides no purpose, dataset provenance, setup instructions, dependency versions, execution procedure, or interpretation of results.
The Analysis section still contains empty numbered placeholders, and the alternative aggregation method is not implemented.

Several plotting cells do not fully satisfy their prompts: one requested regimen plot counts timepoint values instead, the four-regimen comparison is split into separate box plots, and the regression reverses the described predictor and response axes.
There is no dependency manifest, automated test, CI workflow, or reproducibility check.

risks.statement: Saved outputs may not reliably represent the current source cells: execution counts are non-sequential, and the stored output for a cell intended to inspect removed mouse g989 instead begins with records for h246 after applying a mask from a differently indexed DataFrame.
Using the uncleaned master DataFrame for one regimen-count chart can retain duplicate g989 observations and make that visualization inconsistent with later cleaned-data calculations.
Unpinned dependencies and absent source data make future execution sensitive to library changes and prevent independent validation of the committed results.
The repository has no commits after April 2022 and no open issues or pull requests in the supplied snapshot, indicating dormancy rather than ongoing maintenance.

suggested_next_actions.statement: Treat the repository as archived coursework unless the owner expects to reuse the analysis.

If it is retained as a reference, add redistributable input data or documented retrieval instructions, pin the Python environment, restart and run all cells sequentially, and verify that regenerated outputs match the source.
Complete the written conclusions and correct the cleaned-data mask, regimen-count plot, combined box plot, and regression-axis orientation before presenting the notebook as a finished analysis.

questions: Was this repository created as coursework, and is there any reason to preserve it as an active project rather than archive it?
Can the two source CSV files legally be committed, or should the README document where to obtain them?
Were the saved notebook outputs generated from the current cell sources or from an earlier execution state?
Should the repository remain a historical submission, or should correctness and reproducibility issues be repaired?

evidence.summary: Supplied snapshot identifies a public repository on main, last pushed 2022-04-26, with no description, open issues, open pull requests, or issue/PR titles.
The 20-byte README contains only the heading The_Power_of_Plots.

The complete tracked tree contains only .gitignore, README.md, main.ipynb, and pymaceuticals_starter_guided.ipynb; no data, manifest, tests, workflows, docs, releases, or credential files are tracked.
A 36-cell Python notebook with 30 code cells implements a Pymaceuticals mouse-study analysis using pandas, Matplotlib, and SciPy, while retaining several blank or inconsistent exercise sections.
An unexecuted 35-cell guided starter notebook supplies exercise prompts and partial code for the same data-cleaning, statistics, plotting, outlier, and regression workflow.

Twenty-five code cells retain outputs, including 11 inline PNG plots, tabular statistics, outlier results, and a reported correlation of 0.84; no saved error output exists, but execution counts and at least one source/output pairing are inconsistent.

Four commits are visible: an initial commit on 2022-04-09 followed by three generic file-upload commits, ending with main.ipynb on 2022-04-26; only main and origin/main are present and there are no tags.

confidence.rationale: All tracked implementation and available history were inspected, providing strong evidence that this is a dormant notebook analysis prototype. Confidence is reduced because the required datasets are absent, the notebook cannot be independently rerun, saved outputs show execution-state inconsistencies, and live GitHub metadata was inaccessible.

limitations: The missing CSV inputs prevented rerunning or independently validating calculations and charts.
Live GitHub API access failed, so archival state, releases, and remote branch details could not be independently confirmed beyond the supplied snapshot and local refs.
The analysis was constrained to the depth-50 checkout supplied for this task, although local Git reports that the four-commit repository is not shallow.
Saved notebook outputs were inspected as artifacts, not treated as proof that every current source cell executes correctly.
